           Version 0.8 2026-07-12 · Added · 3 entries
          • FortiAnalyzer

          Changed

          • Profile page layout: About first, session details on the account card. Operator request: "About SATOM at the very top; the top-bar banner card across both columns; Active Sessions into the banner with the admin role, plus the last IP connected." The About card is now the first card of the Profile. The account card (name and role) shows the active session, the IP it comes from and when it signed in, the previous sign-in with its date and IP (read from the login rows of the Audit Log; "none recorded" on a first sign-in), and the Sign Out button. The separate Active Sessions card is gone. Branding — Top-bar Banner spans the full width.

          Added

          • Plugin Studio: ask an API about each LB pool member (SOC Search). Operator request: "in the SOC Search diagram, a way to ask an API about the host that appears in the members of the search result" — the API wants a host name. Call an API has a new For each (list) field: one request per item with {{ item }} = that item, duplicates asked once, at most 50 (more is refused, never cut). The answer is a table — the item's columns, Status, Answer, Error — where a host that fails is a row with its error and the others are still asked; only every request failing takes the error arrow. LB: match names to the fleet now saves members (every pool member address once) and _members per row ({ip, port, status}), and DNS: look names up saves ptr ({ip, hostname} for each address with a PTR answer), so a diagram goes members → host names → API.
          • Clone a plugin app: with its data, only its structure, or on the same data as the original. Operator request: "in the plugins section I want them to be clonable; the clone must ask whether everything, or the structure as it is, without the data — and the apps must be able to write in their data section." Plugin Studio → Apps → ⋯ → Clone asks for the new id and name and, for a flow app, what the copy takes: Everything (the structure and the rows of its data stores), Structure only (the same stores and columns, empty) or Same data as the original (no copy: both apps read and write the original's stores, so a row or a column one of them changes, the other sees — "an option to use everything but add more things, with the original's database, so a change is shared"); none is preselected. With Same data the form, diagram and actions are still the copy's own: it can add steps and data stores of its own, and a later change to the original's diagram does not reach it. Every data store only the original uses becomes the clone's own copy and the clone's steps, Save to a data store actions and list fields point at it, so with Everything or Structure only the clone writes its own data and never the original's. Stores other apps use stay shared unless Copy these too is ticked. The clone is a draft (form, diagram, actions, design and images, icon, menu group, ADOMs, access); runs, published versions, automations, sign-in rules and secrets are not copied. Templates from Examples can be cloned. A script app becomes a new Script Library script with the same files and settings (credential values are typed again). One transaction: a refused or failed clone leaves nothing behind. Audited as studio.app.clone.

          • Switch notification categories off for your own account. Operator request: "in the user profile I want to be able to turn off certain notifications, for example config drift." Profile → Notifications has one switch per bell category (Configuration drift, Device health, Signatures, Scheduled automations, SATOM node & HA, Certificates, Backups, Templates & intent, API catalog, Alert engine). A category switched off no longer creates notifications for that user, and its unread ones are marked read (nothing is deleted); every other user's bell is unchanged. It silences the bell, not the finding: drift and the other checks keep running, are audited and are still sent by the e-mail alert rules. Results of your own jobs, bug reports and Wiki notices are always delivered. The Notifications page has a Preferences button and says which categories you muted. The change is audited as profile.notifications.

          • Plugin Studio: Server connections — manage nginx and Apache virtual hosts and their files. Operator request: "a plugin to manage the vhosts of this server and the files inside each one", with "the server must have no access to SATOM". A new connection kind, Server, reaches a Linux web server over SSH as the unprivileged account satom-mon, whose key is installed with restrict,command="satom-webctl": the key opens no shell and can only ask for the operations of satom-webctl (hostctl/, Python standard library, 3.6+): list virtual hosts; read, change, create, enable, disable and delete their configuration; list, read, write, rename, delete files and create folders inside each document root. Every configuration change is backed up and tested with the server's own test, restored when the test fails and reloaded (never restarted) when it passes. SATOM generates the key (never shown), the host key is pinned by an explicit Fetch and trust, writes need Allow writes, and every answer passes the ingestion gate. The installer (install-satom-webctl.sh, downloadable from the connection page) supports Debian, RHEL and SUSE layouts, sets ACLs instead of changing owners, and grants exactly two sudo commands per web server (config test, reload). New flow step Act on a server; scripts call connection(...).server(op, **args). Plugin Studio → Examples → Web hosts installs twelve chained apps (virtual hosts, configuration editor, file browser and editor).

          Fixed

          • A label value over 4 KB no longer makes a metric vanish silently. The metrics store (VictoriaMetrics) drops a whole series when one label value is longer than 4096 bytes, and still answers the write with success, so a collector reported "ok" for a sample that never landed. Values are now cut to fit with a … mark; control characters in a label become spaces; NaN and infinite readings are skipped like any reading the device does not have. No series written so far was affected (checked on both nodes).
          • A device-synced value can no longer blank a plugin page. Plugin data and the Plugin / Lua Studio editors embed JSON in <script> islands that only neutralised </. A value such as a policy comment containing <!--<script> made the browser swallow the rest of the page — the next island, the markup after it and the page's script. Every island now writes <, > and & as JSON escapes (same value to the script, no markup to the browser). The Sentinel "N value(s) away" note no longer bypasses HTML escaping.
          • Sign-ins through the fleet edge are attributed to the client, not to the edge proxy. With two proxies in a row (edge -> local nginx) the forwarded header reaches SATOM as <client>, <edge>, and only the last hop was read, so every operator who came through the edge was audited, and rate-limited, under the edge's address — one shared lockout bucket. The resolver now walks right to left past every hop that is itself a configured trusted proxy (TRUSTED_PROXIES), like nginx real_ip_recursive; the first untrusted hop is the client, and anything a client pre-filled to the left of it is never read. Older audit rows keep the address they were written with.
          • The alert engine no longer counts a bell notice nobody received as delivered. The in-app sink was credited after every write attempt, including one that wrote no row, so a failed write still reported "delivered" and stamped the cooldown. It is now credited only when a notification was written. A finding whose category every administrator muted is listed under in_app_muted (a choice, not a failure) and is not stamped, so the first administrator who switches it back on receives it. The category labels of the Notifications filter, the Troubleshooting guide and the new profile card are now translated (es, de, fr, it).
          • Two people changing the same object no longer overwrite each other without a word. Operator question: "what happens if a user makes the same change on the same object, or on the same sub-object?" Three gaps answered it badly:
          • The edit lock only bound the object editor. Mass Deploy, Processes, Policy Clone, scripts, scheduled actions, the certificate and DNS-decommission jobs and the FortiADC writers changed or deleted an object an operator had open. The lock is now checked where every write reaches the device (the FortiWeb and FortiADC clients, and every FortiGate, FortiAuthenticator, FortiADC and FortiAnalyzer GUI save). A refused write sends nothing, fails its job step with the holder's name and is audited as config.write.edit_locked. A job started by the lock's holder still writes; an unattended run never writes over an open edit. Adding a new object or row is not blocked.
          • The lock belonged to a user, not to a page. One operator with the object open in two tabs overwrote themselves. A lock now belongs to the page that took it: the second tab says "You have this open in another tab or window" and offers Take over. Closing one tab no longer releases the other tab's lock.
          • The last save won. A form loaded before someone else's change sent its old value and nobody was told, whether the change came from another user, a job or the device's own GUI/CLI. Every editor now sends the values it loaded. SATOM reads the object first and refuses a save whose field changed meanwhile, showing what you loaded, what the device holds now and your value. Reload (SATOM's copy is refreshed first) or Overwrite with mine (audited as config.update.overwrote). The same change made twice is not a conflict.
          • The Server Policy page and the GUI dialogs of every product now take the edit lock (only the object editor did), so their saves show who holds it instead of failing on save.
          • A REST API v1 call now writes as its token's owner. The API has no login session, so the edit-lock check saw nobody and refused the owner's own call like an unattended run's.

          Security

          • hostguard: a managed server can never open a connection to SATOM. Both nodes drop every new connection that comes from a server managed through a Server connection (nftables table inet satom_hostguard, loaded by the privileged runner through the new satom-hostguard.path). Replies to the sessions SATOM opens still pass. The list is re-checked as root: SATOM's own nodes, the default gateway, the trusted proxies and the name servers are never blocked. The standby applies the same list after the data sync, and the list is loaded again after a reboot. The same list is enforced at the HTTP layer, before every other gate: a request that reaches SATOM through a reverse proxy (the client address the trusted proxies forward) from a managed server gets 403 Forbidden -- no login page, no API.
          • Servers ADOM, stage 0: the ingestion gate. Groundwork for monitoring Linux and Windows servers: every answer a monitored server gives passes one gate before SATOM uses it — a size cap before parsing, strict JSON (no NaN/Infinity, no duplicate keys, bounded nesting), and a closed schema per reading (memory, filesystems, processes, services) with types, ranges, lengths, character sets and consistency checks. Text with control characters or bidi/zero-width marks is refused, unknown fields are dropped, and one bad value rejects the whole answer. A rejection names the field and the rule, never the value. Every |safe in the templates is now on a reviewed list enforced by a test. No collector uses the gate yet.
